liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Listener finds this track particularly nice, noting the slow and jazzy style [7]
- **Mama Tried** (1 review): This take is called fabulous, extending beyond normal capacity with Garcia shining [10]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): The first set features a perfect performance of this song [9]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Phil's singing on this track is described as unlike anything heard before [8]
- **The Other One** (1 review): This performance is described as absolutely stellar within a solid show [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-01-18.sbd.miller.fix-102444.103186.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 165 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording sounds like B+, with high levels and a strong second set performance [8]
- **gd1979-01-18.nak300.rolfe.miller.100209.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 4.57/5 by 7 [5]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is described as great, attributed to the recording by Charlie Miller; The recording is noted as the fullest and cleanest among the listed options; The recording lacks drums and space, which the listener finds odd [7][10][11]
- **gd1979-01-18.nak300.rolfe.miller.100210.flac24**: source not stated; 22 songs; 172 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [6]. Said about its sound: The recording quality is noted as nice [13]
- **gd1979-01-18.sbd.miller.102444.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 165 min [2]

## Around the show

- Audience members called for Alligator at the beginning, though it was not in rotation [7]
- The attendee remembers snow and cold weather during the show near their 17th birthday [12]
- Listener initially believed this was Keith and Donna's last show before correcting the error [14]
- A naked woman jumped from the front row barrier to the stage edge during intermission [16]
- After landing on her shins, the woman gave a peace sign before roadies removed her [16]
- The second set is described as rocking the entire duration with excellent selections [9]
- Compared to other tour shows, this one is considered middle of the road [11]
- The performance is described as energetic but lackluster overall [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-01-18.sbd.miller.fix-102444.103186.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) -> Cassette (Sony D5) [1]. Also: David Young and Rich Rothenberg provided the tapes for this soundboard recording; Joe B. Jones assisted with the pitch correction for the Jack-A-Roe patch [1]
- **gd1979-01-18.nak300.rolfe.miller.100209.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 300/CP1 -> Cassette Master (Maxell UDXLI/Dolby B) [5]. Also: Steve Rolfe lent the Sennheiser 441 cassette masters for this front-of-house recording; Joe B. Jones helped pitch correct the patch source for The Other One [5]
- **gd1979-01-18.nak300.rolfe.miller.100210.flac24**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 300/CP1 -> Cassette Master (Maxell UDXLI/Dolby B) [6]
- **gd1979-01-18.sbd.miller.102444.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D5) -> Cassette (Sony D5) [2]
